questions.question: Before changing lanes, what should you do?

options.text: Check your side mirror.
Check your rearview mirror.
Turn your head quickly to look for other vehicles.
All of the above.

questions.explanation: Before changing lanes, check both your side and rearview mirrors for traffic behind you. Just before you move into the other lane, quickly look over your shoulder to check for vehicles in your blind spot.

questions.question: If a crossing guard is directing traffic in a school zone, you must:

options.text: Follow the crossing guard's directions.
Do what other cars are doing, even if it goes against the guard's instructions.
Assume the guard should not be directing traffic.
Follow the normal rules as if no children were present.

questions.explanation: Always slow down and be careful when a crossing guard, sign, or police officer tells you to. Always drive slowly and carefully in school zones.

questions.question: You should slow down in which situations?

options.text: On narrow or winding roads.
At intersections or railroad crossings.
When the road is wet or slippery.
All of the above.

questions.explanation: Slow down on narrow or winding roads, near intersections, near railroad crossings, on hills, on sharp or blind curves, where there are pedestrians or hazards, and when roads are wet or slippery.

questions.question: To drive safely at night, you should:

options.text: Stay farther away from the car ahead of you.
Not drive if you are tired.
Make sure your headlights work properly.
All of the above.

questions.explanation: At night, you can see less. Take steps to make night driving safer for yourself and other drivers.

questions.question: Signaling before you turn, change lanes, or leave a curb:

options.text: Is only necessary if other cars are nearby.
Is a good habit and required by law.
Is only necessary during the move, not before.
Is not necessary if you move slowly.

questions.correctAnswerText: Is a good habit and required by law.
questions.explanation: Signal at least 100 feet before turning or changing lanes. Before pulling away from a curb, always signal to warn other drivers.

questions.question: Why is night driving harder than daytime driving?

options.text: Cars overheat faster at night.
You cannot see as well in the dark.
It rains more at night.
You see more motorcycles at night.

questions.correctAnswerText: You cannot see as well in the dark.
questions.explanation: At night, your vision is limited. Always use your headlights. Drive slow enough that you can stop within the distance you can see ahead.

questions.question: When it starts to sleet or snow while you are driving, you should:

options.text: Keep your windshield and mirrors clear.
Leave more space between your car and the car ahead.
Be careful around all other vehicles.
All of the above.

questions.explanation: In snow, keep your windshield and mirrors clear. Increase your distance from other cars because slippery roads make it harder to stop.

questions.question: When you see a steady green traffic light, you should:

options.text: Go through, unless there are vehicles or pedestrians in the intersection.
Stop if a police officer is nearby.
Treat the intersection like a four-way stop.
Come to a complete stop before going.

questions.correctAnswerText: Go through, unless there are vehicles or pedestrians in the intersection.
questions.explanation: At a green light, let pedestrians and vehicles already in the intersection cross first. You can go, but slow down enough to stop if the light changes before you reach the intersection.

questions.question: If you miss your exit on the interstate, you should:

options.text: Quickly cut across traffic to make your turn.
Make a U-turn to go back.
Continue to the next exit.
Put your car in reverse.

questions.explanation: Do not make a sudden turn to catch your exit. If you miss it, go to the next one.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Stop sign ahead.
Lane closed ahead.
Railroad crossing ahead.
Traffic light ahead.

questions.explanation: Warning signs are diamond-shaped with black markings on a yellow background. They warn drivers about upcoming hazards. This sign tells you a traffic light is ahead, so be ready for a yellow or red light.

questions.question: Alcohol:

options.text: Slows your reflexes and reaction time.
Makes you fall asleep.
Wakes you up.
Improves your judgment.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slows your reflexes and reaction time.
questions.explanation: Alcohol slows your brain and reduces your ability to drive safely. It slows your reaction time and impairs your judgment.

questions.question: The most effective safety restraints in a crash are:

options.text: Only a lap and shoulder belt.
Only an airbag.
Both a lap and shoulder belt and an airbag.
No safety restraints.

questions.correctAnswerText: Both a lap and shoulder belt and an airbag.
questions.explanation: Safety belts double your chances of surviving a crash and reduce serious injury. Airbags work best when used with safety belts. Always wear both your shoulder and lap belts.

questions.question: Drinking alcohol and driving is:

options.text: A minor traffic safety problem.
A serious traffic safety problem.
Safe if you have only had a few drinks.
Only dangerous to the driver who drinks.

questions.explanation: Driving while impaired is a serious safety problem. You cannot drive safely if you drink alcohol or use drugs. Impaired driving is dangerous to you and everyone on the road.

questions.question: A person's driving ability can be impaired by:

options.text: Alcohol.
Any medication.
Lack of sleep.
All of the above.

questions.explanation: Safe driving requires the driver to be in good physical condition. Alcohol, legal and illegal drugs, and being tired can all impair your driving.

questions.question: If you notice a vehicle defect that may affect safe operation, you should:

options.text: Fix the defect as soon as possible.
Fix the defect when you can afford it.
Drive at slower speeds.
Drive normally.

questions.correctAnswerText: Fix the defect as soon as possible.
questions.explanation: Fix any defect that may affect safe operation right away. Do not drive the vehicle until the defect is repaired.

questions.question: If an emergency vehicle with flashing lights is near you, you should:

options.text: Speed up to avoid it.
Stop immediately and block its path.
Do everything you can to give it a clear path.
Signal when it is safe for it to pass you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Do everything you can to give it a clear path.
questions.explanation: Give emergency vehicles a clear path. If it is safe, pull to the side of the road to let them pass.

questions.question: When changing lanes, it is important to:

options.text: Signal before you change lanes.
Check your blind spot.
Make sure the lane is clear before entering.
All of the above.

questions.explanation: Signal for enough time before changing lanes or exiting. Look over your shoulder to check your blind spot before moving left or right.

questions.question: You have a green light, but pedestrians are crossing against the red. You should:

options.text: Honk your horn.
Speed up and pass in front of them.
Stop and let them cross safely.
Drive close to scare them away.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop and let them cross safely.
questions.explanation: Let pedestrians cross safely even if you have a green light. Always be careful around pedestrians.

questions.question: Worn or bald tires:

options.text: Make turning more difficult.
Are more likely to hydroplane.
Increase your stopping distance.
All of the above.

questions.explanation: Worn or bald tires increase stopping distance and make turning harder. Tires without good tread also increase the risk of hydroplaning.

questions.question: This road sign means:

options.text: School crossing.
Pedestrian crossing.
Jogging trail.
Busy sidewalk.

questions.explanation: This sign warns you of a pedestrian crossing. Watch for people crossing. Slow down and be ready to stop.

questions.question: What should you do while driving in a travel lane?

options.text: You may stop to drop off passengers.
You may stop to look up an address.
You may make a U-turn or back up if you take the wrong freeway entrance ramp.
Do not stop for any reason. Keep moving until you can safely pull off the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: Do not stop for any reason. Keep moving until you can safely pull off the road.
questions.explanation: Never stop in a travel lane. Keep moving until you can safely pull off the road. If you miss your exit, do not back up. Go to the next exit or find a safe place to turn around.

questions.question: When turning left, you must yield to:

options.text: Other drivers already in the intersection.
Oncoming traffic.
Pedestrians already in the intersection.
All of the above.

questions.explanation: When turning left, you must yield to oncoming traffic, pedestrians, bicyclists, and other drivers already in the intersection.

questions.question: Smoking while driving:

options.text: Does not affect your ability to drive.
Helps you stay alert.
Is a distracting activity.
Is not a distracting activity.

questions.explanation: Smoking while driving distracts you by taking your hands off the wheel and your eyes off the road.

questions.question: If a flagger is directing traffic in a construction zone, you must:

options.text: Follow the flagger's directions.
Do what other drivers are doing, even if the flagger says otherwise.
Assume the flagger should not be there.
Follow the normal traffic laws instead of the flagger's directions.

questions.explanation: Always follow a flagger's directions. Reduce your speed and use caution when directed to do so. Failing to follow a flagger is illegal and dangerous.

questions.question: At an uncontrolled intersection, you arrive at the same time as a vehicle on your right. What should you do?

options.text: Speed up and drive through the intersection.
Slow down and let the vehicle on your right go first.
Drive into the intersection and make the other vehicle stop.
Honk your horn and drive through.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and let the vehicle on your right go first.
questions.explanation: When two vehicles arrive at an uncontrolled intersection at the same time, the vehicle on the right has the right-of-way. Wait until that vehicle passes safely before you go.

questions.question: To cross railroad tracks safely, you should:

options.text: Look both ways only when the red light is flashing.
Listen, look both ways, and cross only if it is safe.
Cross quickly when a train is approaching.
Quickly drive under any lowering gates.

questions.correctAnswerText: Listen, look both ways, and cross only if it is safe.
questions.explanation: Railroad crossings are always dangerous. Look and listen for trains coming from both directions before crossing. Never cross until you are sure it is safe.

questions.question: When driving near a blind pedestrian with a white cane or guide dog, you should:

options.text: Slow down and be ready to stop.
Take the right-of-way.
Drive normally.
Drive away quickly.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and be ready to stop.
questions.explanation: When you see a blind pedestrian with a white cane or guide dog, slow down and give them the right-of-way. Be ready to stop to protect them from injury.

questions.question: If an aggressive driver cuts you off, you should:

options.text: Call the police right away.
Stay calm and move out of their way.
Flash your lights to show they are wrong.
Do something aggressive back to them.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stay calm and move out of their way.
questions.explanation: If an aggressive driver cuts you off, stay calm and get out of their way. Trying to retaliate makes the situation more dangerous.

questions.question: When you leave your vehicle unattended, you must:

options.text: Turn off the engine.
Lock the ignition and remove the key.
Set the parking brake.
All of the above.

questions.explanation: When leaving your vehicle unattended, you must turn off the engine, lock the ignition, remove the key, and set the parking brake.

questions.question: Driving while distracted usually:

options.text: Is never dangerous.
Makes you react more slowly to hazards.
Makes you drive faster.
Is only dangerous for young drivers.

questions.correctAnswerText: Makes you react more slowly to hazards.
questions.explanation: Distractions slow down your reaction time to traffic and hazards. Distracted driving is never safe.

questions.question: How does lack of sleep affect your driving ability compared to other things?

options.text: The same way alcohol does.
The same way amphetamines do.
The same way anger does.
The same way driving with teenagers does.

questions.explanation: Fatigue and alcohol affect your driving in similar ways. Being awake for 18 hours impairs your driving like a blood alcohol level of 0.05 percent. Being awake for 24 hours straight impairs your driving like a blood alcohol level of 0.10 percent.

questions.question: What does a "No standing" sign mean?

options.text: You can never stop your vehicle there.
You can park there if you stay in the vehicle.
You can stop briefly to pick up or drop off passengers.
You can stop to load or unload goods.

questions.correctAnswerText: You can stop briefly to pick up or drop off passengers.
questions.explanation: A "No standing" sign means you can only make a short stop to let passengers in or out.

questions.question: Which statement about speed is true?

options.text: Driving too slowly on some highways can be dangerous.
Speeding can cause death.
Speeding is safe if you are a skilled driver.
Both driving too slowly on some highways can be dangerous and speeding can cause death.

questions.correctAnswerText: Both driving too slowly on some highways can be dangerous and speeding can cause death.
questions.explanation: As speed increases, the risk of death increases. At speeds over 80 miles per hour, you have almost no chance of surviving a crash. Driving slower than other traffic can also be dangerous because other drivers may become impatient and make risky moves to pass you.

questions.question: What is true about drivers who have consumed alcohol before driving?

options.text: They are always aware of the risks they are taking.
They cannot control their bodies, minds, or vehicles properly.
They are better drivers because they are more careful than sober drivers.
They have faster reaction times.

questions.correctAnswerText: They cannot control their bodies, minds, or vehicles properly.
questions.explanation: Alcohol slows down your brain and body. It harms your judgment, vision, concentration, understanding of reality, and reaction time. You should never drive after drinking any amount of alcohol.

questions.question: What do two solid yellow lines on the road mean?

options.text: Passing is allowed from both directions.
Passing is not allowed.
Passing is allowed if you are at the top of a hill.
Passing is allowed during the day only.

questions.explanation: Yellow lines show that traffic on the other side is moving toward you. Never cross two solid yellow lines to pass from either direction.

questions.question: What should you do when you see a railroad crossing warning sign?

options.text: Try to drive faster than the train.
Be ready to stop if a train is near.
Look for a way to drive around lowered gates.
Assume no train is coming and keep driving normally.

questions.correctAnswerText: Be ready to stop if a train is near.
questions.explanation: Railroad crossing warning signs alert you that a train might be coming. Always obey these signs and never try to go around barriers or ignore the warning.

questions.question: You are borrowing a car you have never driven before. What should you do?

options.text: Don't worry because all cars are the same.
Don't tell your friend that you are not familiar with the car.
Ignore any broken equipment so your friend is not embarrassed.
Take a few minutes to learn where everything is and how it works before you drive.

questions.correctAnswerText: Take a few minutes to learn where everything is and how it works before you drive.
questions.explanation: Before driving an unfamiliar car, spend a few minutes finding and testing the turn signals, emergency lights, headlights, windshield wipers, brakes, gear shift, and horn. Fix any broken equipment before driving.

questions.question: What does this road sign mean?

options.text: An intersection is ahead.
A steep hill is ahead.
A winding road is ahead.
Traffic is merging.

questions.explanation: This sign warns you that a steep downhill section is coming.

questions.question: What affects how far your vehicle travels before it stops?

options.text: How fast your vehicle is going.
The condition of your brakes and tires.
The condition of the road.
All of the above.

questions.explanation: Braking distance depends on your speed, the condition of your brakes and tires, and the road surface.

questions.question: Who has the right-of-way at a four-way stop?

options.text: The driver who arrives first.
The driver who arrives last.
One driver should go without stopping.
One driver should wave the other drivers to go first.

questions.explanation: At a four-way stop, all vehicles must stop. The first vehicle to reach the intersection goes first. If two vehicles arrive at the same time, the driver on the right goes first.
